content.content: 1 # UX Method 2 3 4 ## Governing Relations 5 6 This member owns the adopted UX realization process of STDO. It 7 maps [Foundations](FOUNDATIONS.md), the 8 [Transformation Library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) and 9 [Design Module Method](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md). Its own adoption, default 10 coverage, scaffold and exemption clauses determine the covered surface. The 11 common [Spec Method](SPEC_METHOD.md) and 12 [Ticket Method](TICKET_METHOD.md) retain constitutional process and work 13 lifecycle. [ODD Method](ODD_METHOD.md) and 14 [World Model Method](WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md) retain their separate selected 15 carrier and domain meanings. 16 17 Within its adopted surface, apply 18 [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) at the 19 typed input, command-dispatch, replay and closure boundaries. Bind the exact 20 Product contracts, State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub algebras, current owning state, 21 evidence and actual effect/decision grants. Emitting a command supplies no 22 Product-truth or runtime-continuation authority. 23 24 The arguments below use [F1–F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments) 25 within the surface governed by this profile. The Product supplies admitted 26 truth and action contracts; the UX renders that truth, requests changes and 27 receives data across seams it may not control. Stacks offer different state and 28 effect mechanisms. Those instance conditions motivate explicit contracts but 29 do not derive TEA, an accessibility standard or one implementation stack. 30 31 | Determination and consuming law | Conditional argument | Additional UX policy and owner | 32 |---|---|---| 33 | Adoption, ambiguity and scaffolds: [1A](#1a-constitutional-authority-rule), [4A](#4a-process-model-without-language-or-framework-mandate), [13A](#13a-scaffold-and-exemption-law) | Specification ownership binds the governed surface and its purpose (F1/F6). Evidence of a working prototype does not authorize an exception or establish release fitness. An ambiguous case therefore retains the existing authority rule; adopting a stack cannot silently settle its unresolved meaning. | This member chooses TEA within adoption, default covered surfaces and its exact ambiguity exits. An ambiguity exemption uses the design module under 1A; a scaffold exemption uses the design module or ticket under 13A, retaining permitted operations, visible standing, retirement and non-closure conditions. Project realization choices remain within those conditions. | 34 | State transition and projection: [process model](#4-process-model--elm-architecture), [state transition](#5-state-transition-law), [continuation](#8-ux-twin-of-odd-115a--view-does-not-own-continuation) | Information and interpretation distinguish owning state from its view (F2/F3); functional design composes transitions over declared inputs (F4). If losing a supposedly local value changes Product behavior, the view is carrying a material state relation that its projection contract does not own. | This member chooses pure `Update` and `View`, runtime-owned `State`, and the unmount discriminator. Product-meaningful state uses the typed reducer; genuinely view-local ephemera retain their stated permission. | 35 | Commands and observed effects: [state transition](#5-state-transition-law), [effect membrane](#6-effect-membrane-rule) | Computational execution binding distinguishes the command value, dispatch and observed effect. Persistent reality and finite observation (F3/F5) permit lost or partial outcomes, while authority still binds the actual operation (F6). A failure response after dispatch cannot prove no mutation or authorize a blind repeat. | This member chooses typed `Cmd`/`Sub`, a declared interpreter membrane, typed outcome `Msg` cases and deterministic correlation. Shared currentness/effect law decides the observed state and dependent recovery; the membrane acquires no business-continuation authority. | 36 | Product carrier and ingress: [3A](#3a-ux-projection-and-constructive-carrier-boundary), [AssetSurface](#7-assetsurface-binding-rule), [type sharing](#10-type-sharing-rule) | Information and typed composition require compatible meaning at the front/back-end seam (F2/F4); an emitted message cannot grant the operation it names (F6). Consequently a UI-local shape or handler cannot replace an absent Product carrier, and untrusted input cannot become admitted state solely by a compile-time type assertion. | This member chooses shared AssetSurface or named equivalents, one-to-one action bindings or faithful explicit projections, and runtime validation at its declared seams. The Product owns the action contract; the project chooses the schema and interpreter mechanisms. | 37 | Replay proof: [8A](#8a-msg-replay-proof-requirement) | Evidence supports the exact interaction predicate (F1/F2/F6). Functional transitions can be assessed from declared State, ordered Msg/Cmd and deterministic inputs; hidden view state prevents that reconstruction. Faithfully replaying an unknown-effect message establishes the trace relation, not completion of the underlying effect. | This member requires executable proof per product-meaningful interaction family and defines its fixtures, ordered outputs and excluded hidden dependencies. A pure projection may use the declared no-effect proof. Core conjunction retains failed families and missing required coverage. | 38 | Accessibility: [minimum](#11-accessibility-minimum) | Purpose identifies the public capability being exposed (F1), and authority governs its exceptions (F6). That scope distinguishes a public Product surface from a recorded internal debug exemption; a screenshot alone cannot establish interaction obligations. | This member chooses the accessibility minimum and recommended web default. Projects may add stricter refinements. These concrete duties are domain policy, not theorems of finite attention or consequences of passing Msg replay. | 39 | Sprint escrow: [13B](#13b-ux-sprint-compliance-escrow) | Finite work can defer selected proof under an admitted bound (F1/F5), while evidence and authority preserve what remains unproved and who may dispose it (F3/F6). A permitted escrow treatment therefore cannot turn a deferred interaction obligation into completed UX proof. | UX owns the escrow allow/deny boundaries and forensic walkthrough; Ticket owns sprint-close classification and eligibility. Product UX closure still requires its applicable proof. | 40 41 Applicable Design Module and UX obligations 42 conjoin at their actual closure consumer using the shared 43 [result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) and 44 [result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction). 45 46 47 48 ## 1. Position 49 50 `UX_METHOD.md` exists to make one instruction precise: 51 52 `using UX_METHOD, build this UI surface` 53 54 The method adopts the **Elm Architecture (TEA)** as its constitutional process model: 55 56 - the view is a pure projection of typed state 57 - state transitions are pure reductions over typed messages 58 - side effects are values described by the reducer and interpreted at a declared effect membrane 59 - the runtime owns lifecycle; the view does not own continuation 60 61 The view is not a state owner. 62 63 Stateful local mutation in views, two-way bindings without action emission, and effect-handlers-as-controllers are method violations even when they are conventionally accepted in the surrounding ecosystem. 64 65 ### 1A. Constitutional Authority Rule 66 67 When a product, ticket, design module, or review adopts this method for a UX 68 surface, `UX_METHOD.md` is the sole UX realization authority for that surface. 69 70 Project-local ADRs may choose the stack. They may not weaken the process model. 71 72 Existing code, component-library convention, screenshots, comments, design 73 history, prototype behavior, and generated artifacts are evidence only. They do 74 not override this method. 75 76 If this method appears ambiguous in a concrete case, the surface fails closed: 77 the work must either satisfy the stricter interpretation, reprice through the 78 governing constitutional method, or record a scoped exemption in the design 79 module before implementation proceeds. 80 81 --- 82 83 ## 2. Method Role 84 85 `SPEC_METHOD.md` defines constitutional process and lawful re-entry. 86 87 `ODD_METHOD.md` defines graph-native constructive carrier law. 88 89 `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` defines deterministic module-level realization discipline. 90 91 `UX_METHOD.md` refines `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` with the additional rules required when a module realizes a UX surface — render purity, state-transition algebra, effect-membrane discipline, and accessibility minimums — under the Elm Architecture process model. 92 93 `UX_METHOD.md` does not duplicate `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`. Where the parent method already governs (immutability, totality, effect-edge discipline, no-semantic-center, coupling), `UX_METHOD.md` cites and extends it. Where UX has concerns the parent does not address (render lifecycle, browser events, layout, accessibility), `UX_METHOD.md` is authoritative. 94 95 --- 96 97 ## 3. Method Composition 98 99 `UX_METHOD.md` composes with the upstream methods on a per-surface basis: 100 101 - when a module realizes a UX surface, both `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` and `UX_METHOD.md` apply 102 - when a module realizes a non-UX surface, only `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` applies 103 - when an ODD product publishes a projection / query surface that includes UX (`§10` of `ODD_METHOD.md`), `UX_METHOD.md` governs that surface's realization 104 105 The composition rule is: 106 107 - `ODD_METHOD.md` answers what graph-native shape the product takes 108 - `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` answers what realization discipline the modules follow 109 - `UX_METHOD.md` answers what additional discipline UX surfaces follow 110 111 ### 3A. UX Projection And Constructive Carrier Boundary 112 113 UX surfaces are projection and control surfaces. They render admitted truth and 114 emit typed messages. 115 116 A UX-local `Msg` may govern view-local concerns such as expansion state, sort 117 order, filter text, focus movement, or draft input. 118 119 A UX `Msg` that changes product truth is not merely a UX concern. Product-truth 120 changes include: 121 122 - writing, creating, moving, or deleting assets 123 - changing Context, selection authority, pinning, or global product state 124 - spawning, attaching, or resuming sessions 125 - dispatching agents, jobs, workorders, graph calls, or runtime commands 126 - changing closure, approval, continuation, lineage, provenance, or evidence 127 - publishing, accepting, rejecting, or superseding product records 128 129 Such a message must map to one admitted product carrier: 130 131 - an `AssetSurface` action 132 - a published graph function or lawful graph-function composition 133 - a workorder, job, or runtime command admitted by the product's design 134 - an ABG event or command boundary where ABG is the runtime authority 135 - another typed product contract named by the design module 136 137 The UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. If no admitted 138 carrier exists for a product-truth-changing message, the UX surface is blocked 139 until the carrier is authored or the requirement is repriced. 140 141 --- 142 143 144 145 ## 4. Process Model — Elm Architecture 146 147 The constitutional process model is the Elm Architecture: 148 149 - **State** — typed state shape held by the runtime, not by the view 150 - **Msg** — typed message algebra naming every action a user or system can emit 151 - **Update** — pure reducer of signature `(Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`; describes side effects as `Cmd` values, does not perform them 152 - **View** — pure function of signature `State → ViewTree`; given the same state, produces the same output 153 - **Cmd / Sub** — typed descriptions of side effects to schedule and external sources to subscribe to; interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane 154 155 The runtime owns the loop: 156 157 `current State → render View → user emits Msg → Update produces new State and Cmds → runtime interprets Cmds → repeat` 158 159 This loop is the Elm Architecture. It is the constitutional process model of UX work under this method. 160 161 --- 162 163 ## 4A. Process Model Without Language Or Framework Mandate 164 165 The process model is the Elm Architecture. The implementation stack is the project's choice, recorded in the project's design module. 166 167 This mirrors `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` §4 ("Functional Bias Without Language Mandate"). The rule is: 168 169 - the **process model** is constitutional and not negotiable 170 - the **stack** is project-local and free, provided it preserves the model 171 172 Any realization that preserves §4–§8 is method-compliant. Examples (non-normative): 173 174 - **A language-integrated reducer runtime** — enables typed state, message, 175 update, command, and view relations as native runtime capabilities. 176 - **A typed reducer with an effect interpreter** — enables a host-language UI 177 stack to preserve pure update and an explicit effect membrane. 178 - **A reactive-signal realization behind a reducer** — enables reactive 179 projection while forbidding signal mutation outside the reducer. 180 - **A server-rendered hypermedia realization** — enables server-side state 181 derivation as the reducer and uses the request/response boundary as the 182 effect membrane. 183 184 What is constitutionally rejected: any realization that lets the view own state continuation, performs side effects in render code, mutates state outside a typed reducer, or carries multi-step view-local state machines that bypass `Msg`. Two-way binding without `Msg` emission, imperative DOM manipulation in render code, and effect-handlers used as controllers are violations regardless of stack. 185 186 A project that selects a framework records the choice in its design module along with a short justification of how the framework preserves the §4 process model. The method does not rank frameworks. The method tests realizations against §4–§8. 187 188 --- 189 190 ## 5. State Transition Law 191 192 State changes through typed messages applied by the pure reducer (`Update` of §4). 193 194 A UX surface declares: 195 196 - its `State` shape 197 - its `Msg` algebra 198 - its `Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)` 199 - its `Cmd` algebra 200 - its `Sub` algebra when the surface subscribes to external or runtime events 201 202 Each `Cmd` declaration names: 203 204 - the effect kind 205 - the typed input payload 206 - the admitted carrier or external boundary it targets 207 - the typed outcome `Msg` family returned to the reducer, including every 208 observed or unresolved effect case possible under the command contract (§6) 209 - the reason and observation carried by each case; a success/failure label alone 210 does not establish completion or absence of effects 211 - any deterministic correlation key required for replay 212 213 The reducer is pure. It does not perform I/O, log to side channels, or mutate global state. Effects scheduled by `Cmd` are interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane (see §6). 214 215 View-local ephemera (open/closed flags, hover state, draft input) may be held in implementation-local state cells where the framework provides them, but only when the value is genuinely view-local (not observed by other views, not part of the product's state surface, not consequential after the view unmounts). Product-meaningful state goes through the reducer without exception. 216 217 The discipline test for whether state belongs in the reducer or in view-local ephemera: if losing the value on unmount changes the product's behavior or another part of the UI's view, it belongs in the reducer. 218 219 --- 220 221 ## 6. Effect Membrane Rule 222 223 Side effects are isolated to a declared effect membrane. 224 225 The membrane interprets `Cmd` values produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into `Msg` values delivered to the reducer. 226 227 Inside the membrane: 228 229 - I/O is allowed 230 - subscriptions to external sources are allowed 231 - imperative interop with the host platform is allowed (DOM, file system, native APIs) 232 233 Outside the membrane (in render code, in pure helpers consumed by render, in the reducer): 234 235 - no I/O 236 - no subscriptions 237 - no imperative platform manipulation 238 239 The membrane has one job: interpret declared `Cmd` values. It is not where logic lives. Branching, conditional state derivation, and multi-step business decisions belong in the reducer; the membrane interprets a single declared `Cmd` per effect. 240 241 Effect returns distinguish each shared effect state the command can produce 242 as typed `Msg` cases under its contract, including observed non-start and 243 reversal where applicable. The method result 244 records the corresponding shared effect state under the single 245 [effect observation law](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra); it does not replace 246 the UX domain's message algebra. The command binding relates each qualified 247 message to that observation boundary and evidence, preserving missing-reason 248 and unknown cases rather than guessing from a message name. A failed response after dispatch can mean `unknown` 249 effects, not proof of no mutation. Before a dependent repeat, the declared 250 recovery command observes the actual owning state. Reconstructed UI context or 251 an old success message cannot override that observation. This applies 252 [workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) without turning 253 the effect membrane into a second continuation controller. 254 255 A platform-specific effect handler (whatever name the chosen framework gives it: `useEffect`, `createEffect`, `onMount`, `subscribe`, server-action handler) is part of the membrane only when it interprets a declared `Cmd`. A handler that contains conditional logic deciding state transitions is a method violation. Move the logic to the reducer; let the handler interpret one `Cmd`. 256 257 --- 258 259 ## 7. AssetSurface Binding Rule 260 261 When the product publishes typed asset surfaces (per `ODD_METHOD.md` §11 carrier law and the local product's design), a UX surface binds to one or more `AssetSurface` contracts as its data source and action target. 262 263 Binding requirements: 264 265 - the UX surface's `State` is derived from `AssetSurface` projections, not from a UX-local re-declaration of the asset shape 266 - the UX surface's product-truth-changing `Msg` variants map one-to-one to `AssetSurface` action-registry entries or wrap them through a documented projection with no hidden semantic change 267 - UX-local `Msg` variants are reserved for view-local concerns (open/closed, sort order, filter input) 268 - selection within the UX surface emits a Context update (or equivalent) consistent with the product's selection contract 269 - writes from the UX surface go through the `AssetSurface` action registry, not through direct file or service calls 270 271 This is the rule that produces strong functional consistency between front-end and back-end: the same typed contract is the ground truth on both sides. 272 273 If the product does not publish `AssetSurface` contracts, the design module must 274 name the equivalent typed contract and apply the same binding law to that 275 contract. Absence of an admitted contract blocks product-truth-changing UX 276 actions. 277 278 --- 279 280 281 282 ## 8. UX Twin Of ODD §11.5A — View Does Not Own Continuation 283 284 `ODD_METHOD.md` §11.5A states that ABG owns continuation; the product is a cooperative bounded-step subsystem. 285 286 The UX twin: **the view does not own state continuation.** 287 288 State transitions flow through declared `Msg` actions interpreted by the reducer. A view does not: 289 290 - decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event 291 - chain multiple state updates locally without emitting them as separate `Msg` values 292 - carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures, or module-level variables 293 294 If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that state machine belongs in the reducer as part of `State`, with explicit `Msg` transitions between phases. The view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is in. 295 296 The discipline test is the **Msg-replay test**: can you replay the view's behavior by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State`? If the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view. 297 298 ### 8A. Msg-Replay Proof Requirement 299 300 Every product UX surface must carry at least one executable Msg-replay proof for 301 each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming method closure. 302 303 A replay proof includes: 304 305 - an initial `State` fixture 306 - an ordered `Msg` log 307 - the expected final `State` 308 - the expected ordered `Cmd` values 309 - the typed outcome `Msg` values returned by interpreted `Cmd`s, including 310 unresolved effects wherever admitted by the interaction contract 311 - injected deterministic values for time, randomness, generated ids, and 312 external payloads 313 314 The proof fails if correctness depends on: 315 316 - DOM state not represented in `State` 317 - mutable refs, module variables, closures, timers, or effect-handler memory 318 - network or file results that bypass typed `Msg` 319 - view-local state that changes product behavior after unmount or replay 320 321 For a pure projection-only surface, the replay proof may be a no-effect proof: 322 `Msg` log plus final `State` and empty `Cmd` sequence. 323 324 Each replay assessment returns the shared 325 [result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) on the exact interaction-family 326 predicate, preserving the original test outcome and observed command/effect 327 trace. Evidence of the expected final State, ordered Cmds and typed returns 328 under the declared replay conditions satisfies that replay predicate. 329 A replay can correctly reproduce an unknown-effect Msg without establishing 330 completion of the underlying effect. A demonstrated expected-state or command 331 mismatch, or a demonstrated dependency on any source excluded by this replay 332 contract, is `falsified`; a 333 proof not run retains `not_performed` and cannot satisfy the predicate. 334 Missing decisive trace is `indeterminate`; an unusable fixture or governing 335 basis is `invalid_basis`; an interaction outside the declared assessment domain 336 is `out_of_frame`. Conjoin the required family assessments and other applicable 337 closure checks through [result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction), 338 retaining failed families and missing coverage. An empty command sequence proves 339 the no-effect predicate only when that is the declared interaction contract. 340 341 --- 342 343 ## 9. View Shape Rule 344 345 A view is a pure function from typed state to a view tree. 346 347 The view: 348 349 - accepts typed input (state, props, context) 350 - returns a typed view tree 351 - declares its consumed inputs explicitly 352 - does not capture mutable state in closures across renders 353 - does not read from sources outside its declared input 354 355 Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived expression, or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body. 356 357 A view that depends on out-of-render mutation (e.g., a ref written from inside an effect handler and read during render) is a method violation under §6 unless the mutation is part of the declared effect membrane (e.g., a platform handle for imperative interop already named in the design module). 358 359 --- 360 361 ## 10. Type Sharing Rule 362 363 UX-consumed types come from the shared front-end / back-end contract. 364 365 A UX surface does not re-declare back-end record shapes. It imports them from the shared contract module (typically the same package or a dedicated `contracts/` package). 366 367 Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam: 368 369 - HTTP or RPC responses 370 - MCP payloads 371 - file-loaded records 372 - websocket or event-stream messages 373 - agent or worker outputs 374 - URL, storage, clipboard, or browser integration payloads 375 376 The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so the same type definition is the 377 source of both compile-time types and runtime validators. The mechanism choice 378 is project-local. Compile-time TypeScript alone is not sufficient at these 379 seams. 380 381 UX-local types are allowed for view-local concerns: form input draft state, sort order enums, filter strings. UX-local types do not shadow back-end types. 382 383 --- 384 385 ## 11. Accessibility Minimum 386 387 A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares: 388 389 - semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or platform-equivalent affordances) 390 - keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has a pointer interaction 391 - focus management on dynamic content changes 392 - accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks a native semantic equivalent 393 - color contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG AA is the recommended default for web) 394 395 Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional for internal-only debug surfaces; the design module records the exemption. 396 397 This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it from their design modules. 398 399 --- 400 401 ## 12. Realization Discretion 402 403 The method is opinionated about the process model. It is not opinionated about the realization stack. 404 405 The project chooses: 406 407 - the language 408 - the framework or runtime 409 - the state-container library (if any) 410 - the effect-interpreter mechanism 411 - the runtime validator (if any) 412 - the build, bundling, and deployment toolchain 413 414 The project records its choices in the design module along with a short justification of how each choice preserves the §4 Elm process model and the §6 effect-membrane rule. 415 416 The method does not rank stacks. It tests realizations. A realization is method-compliant when §4–§10 hold under inspection and the §14 failure patterns are absent. 417 418 --- 419 420 ## 13. Adoption Guidance 421 422 A project adopts `UX_METHOD.md` by: 423 424 1. naming the method in the project's UX-related design modules 425 2. recording the realization stack choice (per §12) and the justification 426 3. declaring the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set and structural carrier 427 diagram required by `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` 428 4. declaring the `State`, `Msg`, `Update`, `Cmd`, and `Sub` shapes for each UX 429 surface in the design module before implementation 430 5. declaring the `AssetSurface` or equivalent typed-contract bindings (per §7) 431 the surface consumes and emits to 432 6. naming the effect-membrane mechanism (per §6) and the `Cmd` algebra it 433 interprets 434 7. naming the executable Msg-replay proof surface required by §8A 435 8. naming any §11 accessibility refinement the project requires 436 9. noting any §9 view-shape or §6 effect-membrane exemptions explicitly 437 438 Adoption is per-project. A project may adopt this method only for some UX surfaces (e.g., the production UI but not internal debug tools), with the scope recorded in the design module. 439 440 ### 13A. Scaffold And Exemption Law 441 442 A UX surface is governed by this method by default when any of these are true: 443 444 - it is reachable from the product shell 445 - it is used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release, or 446 review 447 - it can mutate product truth 448 - it can spawn, attach, resume, or dispatch work 449 - it can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence, 450 or provenance 451 452 A scaffold, prototype, debug pane, or temporary proof surface may be exempt only 453 when the design module or ticket records: 454 455 - the exemption scope 456 - the permitted operations 457 - whether mutation is forbidden or explicitly bounded 458 - a visible scaffold/debug label where user-facing 459 - the authoritative surface that will supersede it 460 - the retirement condition and owning ticket 461 - the non-closure condition preventing release if the scaffold remains 462 463 An exempt scaffold cannot become the production UX by accumulation. It must be 464 retired, repriced into a governed UX surface, or kept outside product closure. 465 466 ### 13B. UX Sprint Compliance Escrow 467 468 UX is the primary governed use case for sprint compliance escrow. 469 470 Under `SPEC_METHOD.md` and `TICKET_METHOD.md`, a UX sprint may defer local UX 471 compliance proof during a short iteration window when per-change proof cost is 472 higher than expected correction cost. 473 474 This is a cost-optimization rule. It does not weaken the UX process model. 475 476 A UX sprint may escrow: 477 478 - screenshots or walkthrough capture 479 - visual review 480 - copy, spacing, density, and layout cleanup 481 - accessibility review and remediation 482 - Msg-replay proof updates for product-meaningful interaction families 483 - design-module wording cleanup 484 - trace cleanup between changed UX states and governing authority 485 486 A UX sprint may not escrow: 487 488 - product-truth-changing `Msg` variants that lack an admitted carrier 489 - new or changed `AssetSurface` contracts or equivalent typed product contracts 490 - new navigation, information architecture, or selection authority that changes 491 product meaning 492 - runtime, governance, closure, continuation, lineage, provenance, or evidence 493 semantics 494 - release criteria or method law 495 496 If one of those appears, the sprint records the finding and the work exits the 497 UX sprint path through standalone repricing or sprint supersession. The UX layer 498 must still not become the hidden constructive carrier. 499 500 A UX sprint should close when continued iteration is more expensive or less 501 trustworthy than review. Valid close triggers include: 502 503 - the declared timebox ends 504 - accumulated changed states are too numerous for casual review 505 - screenshots or walkthrough evidence no longer explain the current surface 506 - interaction behavior changed beyond visual polish 507 - reviewer uncertainty makes more iteration unsafe without reconciliation 508 509 UX sprint close is a forensic walkthrough. The walkthrough reviews each changed 510 screen, state, and product-meaningful interaction against the cited authority. 511 512 Classify each finding under 513 [Ticket Sprint Close Review](TICKET_METHOD.md#sprint-close-review), which owns 514 the six treatment classes and their reason-sensitive assessment/decision 515 bindings. The UX item-compliance predicate is "this changed screen, state or 516 product-meaningful interaction meets the applicable UX Method and cited design 517 obligations at this basis." Bind its current surface, adopted scope, 518 applicability/exemption evidence and the exact obligations to that owner's 519 map. Apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) 520 to the admissibility of this assessment and support; assess UX compliance 521 separately. The treatment and its competent decision authority cannot replace 522 that assessment. Retain the actual failure, uncertainty, performance and 523 effects, including when a local paydown or removal treatment is lawful. 524 525 Sprint-close eligibility and product UX method closure are separate predicates. 526 The former admits local paydown only under its stated policy. The latter 527 requires its applicable replay and accessibility proof through core conjunction. 528 A recorded authorised exemption decides only its named applicability; an 529 unrecorded exemption supplies no such evidence. Closing the sprint establishes 530 neither discharge of paydown nor method closure. 531 532 The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where the debt is 533 local to UX realization and the governing method allows follow-up. It may not 534 close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden state continuation, or authority 535 drift remain unclassified. 536 537 Method closure for a product UX surface still requires the §8A Msg-replay proof 538 and §11 accessibility obligations unless an explicit exemption is recorded. The 539 sprint can defer those obligations during iteration; it cannot erase them. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## 14. Failure Pattern 544 545 A UX surface is violating this method when any of these are true: 546 547 1. render code mutates state directly (assignments inside the render body, mutating a prop or context value) 548 2. view-local state cells carry product-meaningful state instead of view-local ephemera 549 3. an effect handler contains conditional logic that decides state transitions 550 4. multi-step state machines live in the view rather than in the reducer 551 5. mutable refs are read during render outside the declared effect membrane 552 6. UX-local types shadow or re-declare back-end types instead of importing from the shared contract 553 7. selection or action emission writes to file or network without going through an `AssetSurface` action 554 8. view-shape exemptions (per §9) are taken without a recorded design-module entry 555 9. accessibility is omitted on a public product capability without a recorded exemption 556 10. two-way binding emits no typed `Msg` action and the reducer is bypassed 557 11. logic that should be a `Cmd` is implemented imperatively inside an effect handler 558 12. the view's behavior cannot be replayed by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State` 559 13. a product-truth-changing UX message has no admitted carrier, graph function, runtime command, or typed product contract 560 14. external data crosses into UX state without runtime validation 561 15. a scaffold or debug surface is reachable, mutating, or used as proof without the §13A exemption record 562 16. a project-local ADR, component convention, or existing code pattern is used to weaken this method 563 17. a UX sprint claims closure while deferred proof, accessibility, carrier, 564 scaffold, or authority debt remains unclassified or un-ticketed 565 566 Any of these is a method violation. Repeated violations are not normalized by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced. 567 568 --- 569 570 ## 15. Review Questions 571 572 A UX surface review under this method should answer: 573 574 1. What is the surface's `State`, `Msg`, and `Update`? 575 2. What is the surface's `Cmd` and `Sub` algebra? 576 3. Which `AssetSurface` or equivalent typed contracts does it bind to? 577 4. Which product-truth-changing messages map to admitted carriers? 578 5. Where is the effect membrane, and what `Cmd` values does it interpret? 579 6. Is `View = f(State)` provably pure for this surface? 580 7. Can the surface's behavior be replayed from a `Msg` log (the §8A Msg-replay proof)? 581 8. Are all UX-consumed types imported from the shared contract? 582 9. Are all out-of-process payloads runtime-validated before entering UX state? 583 10. Are view-shape, effect-membrane, accessibility, scaffold, or debug exemptions documented? 584 11. What realization stack is chosen, and how does it preserve the §4 Elm process model? 585 12. Does the surface honor the §8 view-does-not-own-continuation rule under user replay? 586 13. Does the design module include the `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` carrier set and structural carrier diagram required for closure? 587 14. If the work used a UX sprint, did close review classify every deferred proof, 588 accessibility, carrier, scaffold, and authority finding? 589 590 If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete. 591 592 --- 593 594 ## 16. Relationship To Other Method Surfaces 595 596 - `SPEC_METHOD.md` governs constitutional process, authority flow, repricing, and migration law. 597 - `ODD_METHOD.md` governs graph-native constructive carrier law. UX surfaces are projection / query surfaces under §10 of that method. 598 - `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` governs deterministic realization discipline at the module level. `UX_METHOD.md` refines it for UX modules. 599 - `TICKET_METHOD.md` governs ticket and sprint lifecycle. UX work may use sprint compliance escrow under §13B when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof visible, bounded, and payable. 600 - `WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` governs world-model semantic law for products that have a world-model dimension. UX surfaces over world-model state still bind through `AssetSurface` (or equivalent) per §7. 601 602 A UX-touching design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` plus `UX_METHOD.md`. A non-UX design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` only and ignores this surface. 603 604 --- 605 606 ## 17. Non-Goals 607 608 `UX_METHOD.md` is not: 609 610 - a styling guide or design system specification 611 - a component library 612 - a brand or visual-identity surface 613 - a wireframing or prototyping process 614 - a research method for user studies 615 - a stack ranking or framework recommendation 616 617 Those are valid concerns; they belong in product-local surfaces, not in this constitutional method. 618 619 --- 620 621 ## 18. Canonical Compression 622 623 `UX_METHOD.md` adopts the **Elm Architecture** as the constitutional UX process model and refines `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` for UX surfaces. The model: typed `State` held by the runtime, typed `Msg` algebra, pure `Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`, pure `View : State → ViewTree`, side effects as `Cmd` values interpreted at a declared effect membrane that returns `Msg` to the reducer. The view does not own continuation (UX twin of `ODD_METHOD.md` §11.5A); the **Msg-replay test** is the discipline check. The realization stack is the project's choice, recorded in the design module along with justification of model preservation. The method tests realizations against §4–§10 and the §14 failure patterns; it does not rank stacks, languages, or frameworks. 624 625 When adopted, this method is the sole UX realization authority for the covered 626 surface. Product-truth-changing UX messages must map to admitted product 627 carriers; the UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. External 628 payloads are runtime-validated before entering UX state. Scaffolds and debug 629 surfaces are governed unless explicitly exempted, bounded, and retired. UX 630 sprints may defer local proof and cleanup only as visible compliance escrow; 631 close review must classify and pay down the debt before method closure is 632 claimed. 633

file.content: # UX Method ## Governing Relations This member owns the adopted UX realization process of STDO. It maps [Foundations](FOUNDATIONS.md), the [Transformation Library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) and [Design Module Method](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md). Its own adoption, default coverage, scaffold and exemption clauses determine the covered surface. The common [Spec Method](SPEC_METHOD.md) and [Ticket Method](TICKET_METHOD.md) retain constitutional process and work lifecycle. [ODD Method](ODD_METHOD.md) and [World Model Method](WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md) retain their separate selected carrier and domain meanings. Within its adopted surface, apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) at the typed input, command-dispatch, replay and closure boundaries. Bind the exact Product contracts, State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub algebras, current owning state, evidence and actual effect/decision grants. Emitting a command supplies no Product-truth or runtime-continuation authority. The arguments below use [F1–F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments) within the surface governed by this profile. The Product supplies admitted truth and action contracts; the UX renders that truth, requests changes and receives data across seams it may not control. Stacks offer different state and effect mechanisms. Those instance conditions motivate explicit contracts but do not derive TEA, an accessibility standard or one implementation stack. | Determination and consuming law | Conditional argument | Additional UX policy and owner | |---|---|---| | Adoption, ambiguity and scaffolds: [1A](#1a-constitutional-authority-rule), [4A](#4a-process-model-without-language-or-framework-mandate), [13A](#13a-scaffold-and-exemption-law) | Specification ownership binds the governed surface and its purpose (F1/F6). Evidence of a working prototype does not authorize an exception or establish release fitness. An ambiguous case therefore retains the existing authority rule; adopting a stack cannot silently settle its unresolved meaning. | This member chooses TEA within adoption, default covered surfaces and its exact ambiguity exits. An ambiguity exemption uses the design module under 1A; a scaffold exemption uses the design module or ticket under 13A, retaining permitted operations, visible standing, retirement and non-closure conditions. Project realization choices remain within those conditions. | | State transition and projection: [process model](#4-process-model--elm-architecture), [state transition](#5-state-transition-law), [continuation](#8-ux-twin-of-odd-115a--view-does-not-own-continuation) | Information and interpretation distinguish owning state from its view (F2/F3); functional design composes transitions over declared inputs (F4). If losing a supposedly local value changes Product behavior, the view is carrying a material state relation that its projection contract does not own. | This member chooses pure `Update` and `View`, runtime-owned `State`, and the unmount discriminator. Product-meaningful state uses the typed reducer; genuinely view-local ephemera retain their stated permission. | | Commands and observed effects: [state transition](#5-state-transition-law), [effect membrane](#6-effect-membrane-rule) | Computational execution binding distinguishes the command value, dispatch and observed effect. Persistent reality and finite observation (F3/F5) permit lost or partial outcomes, while authority still binds the actual operation (F6). A failure response after dispatch cannot prove no mutation or authorize a blind repeat. | This member chooses typed `Cmd`/`Sub`, a declared interpreter membrane, typed outcome `Msg` cases and deterministic correlation. Shared currentness/effect law decides the observed state and dependent recovery; the membrane acquires no business-continuation authority. | | Product carrier and ingress: [3A](#3a-ux-projection-and-constructive-carrier-boundary), [AssetSurface](#7-assetsurface-binding-rule), [type sharing](#10-type-sharing-rule) | Information and typed composition require compatible meaning at the front/back-end seam (F2/F4); an emitted message cannot grant the operation it names (F6). Consequently a UI-local shape or handler cannot replace an absent Product carrier, and untrusted input cannot become admitted state solely by a compile-time type assertion. | This member chooses shared AssetSurface or named equivalents, one-to-one action bindings or faithful explicit projections, and runtime validation at its declared seams. The Product owns the action contract; the project chooses the schema and interpreter mechanisms. | | Replay proof: [8A](#8a-msg-replay-proof-requirement) | Evidence supports the exact interaction predicate (F1/F2/F6). Functional transitions can be assessed from declared State, ordered Msg/Cmd and deterministic inputs; hidden view state prevents that reconstruction. Faithfully replaying an unknown-effect message establishes the trace relation, not completion of the underlying effect. | This member requires executable proof per product-meaningful interaction family and defines its fixtures, ordered outputs and excluded hidden dependencies. A pure projection may use the declared no-effect proof. Core conjunction retains failed families and missing required coverage. | | Accessibility: [minimum](#11-accessibility-minimum) | Purpose identifies the public capability being exposed (F1), and authority governs its exceptions (F6). That scope distinguishes a public Product surface from a recorded internal debug exemption; a screenshot alone cannot establish interaction obligations. | This member chooses the accessibility minimum and recommended web default. Projects may add stricter refinements. These concrete duties are domain policy, not theorems of finite attention or consequences of passing Msg replay. | | Sprint escrow: [13B](#13b-ux-sprint-compliance-escrow) | Finite work can defer selected proof under an admitted bound (F1/F5), while evidence and authority preserve what remains unproved and who may dispose it (F3/F6). A permitted escrow treatment therefore cannot turn a deferred interaction obligation into completed UX proof. | UX owns the escrow allow/deny boundaries and forensic walkthrough; Ticket owns sprint-close classification and eligibility. Product UX closure still requires its applicable proof. | Applicable Design Module and UX obligations conjoin at their actual closure consumer using the shared [result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) and [result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction). ## 1. Position `UX_METHOD.md` exists to make one instruction precise: `using UX_METHOD, build this UI surface` The method adopts the **Elm Architecture (TEA)** as its constitutional process model: - the view is a pure projection of typed state - state transitions are pure reductions over typed messages - side effects are values described by the reducer and interpreted at a declared effect membrane - the runtime owns lifecycle; the view does not own continuation The view is not a state owner. Stateful local mutation in views, two-way bindings without action emission, and effect-handlers-as-controllers are method violations even when they are conventionally accepted in the surrounding ecosystem. ### 1A. Constitutional Authority Rule When a product, ticket, design module, or review adopts this method for a UX surface, `UX_METHOD.md` is the sole UX realization authority for that surface. Project-local ADRs may choose the stack. They may not weaken the process model. Existing code, component-library convention, screenshots, comments, design history, prototype behavior, and generated artifacts are evidence only. They do not override this method. If this method appears ambiguous in a concrete case, the surface fails closed: the work must either satisfy the stricter interpretation, reprice through the governing constitutional method, or record a scoped exemption in the design module before implementation proceeds. --- ## 2. Method Role `SPEC_METHOD.md` defines constitutional process and lawful re-entry. `ODD_METHOD.md` defines graph-native constructive carrier law. `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` defines deterministic module-level realization discipline. `UX_METHOD.md` refines `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` with the additional rules required when a module realizes a UX surface — render purity, state-transition algebra, effect-membrane discipline, and accessibility minimums — under the Elm Architecture process model. `UX_METHOD.md` does not duplicate `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`. Where the parent method already governs (immutability, totality, effect-edge discipline, no-semantic-center, coupling), `UX_METHOD.md` cites and extends it. Where UX has concerns the parent does not address (render lifecycle, browser events, layout, accessibility), `UX_METHOD.md` is authoritative. --- ## 3. Method Composition `UX_METHOD.md` composes with the upstream methods on a per-surface basis: - when a module realizes a UX surface, both `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` and `UX_METHOD.md` apply - when a module realizes a non-UX surface, only `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` applies - when an ODD product publishes a projection / query surface that includes UX (`§10` of `ODD_METHOD.md`), `UX_METHOD.md` governs that surface's realization The composition rule is: - `ODD_METHOD.md` answers what graph-native shape the product takes - `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` answers what realization discipline the modules follow - `UX_METHOD.md` answers what additional discipline UX surfaces follow ### 3A. UX Projection And Constructive Carrier Boundary UX surfaces are projection and control surfaces. They render admitted truth and emit typed messages. A UX-local `Msg` may govern view-local concerns such as expansion state, sort order, filter text, focus movement, or draft input. A UX `Msg` that changes product truth is not merely a UX concern. Product-truth changes include: - writing, creating, moving, or deleting assets - changing Context, selection authority, pinning, or global product state - spawning, attaching, or resuming sessions - dispatching agents, jobs, workorders, graph calls, or runtime commands - changing closure, approval, continuation, lineage, provenance, or evidence - publishing, accepting, rejecting, or superseding product records Such a message must map to one admitted product carrier: - an `AssetSurface` action - a published graph function or lawful graph-function composition - a workorder, job, or runtime command admitted by the product's design - an ABG event or command boundary where ABG is the runtime authority - another typed product contract named by the design module The UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. If no admitted carrier exists for a product-truth-changing message, the UX surface is blocked until the carrier is authored or the requirement is repriced. --- ## 4. Process Model — Elm Architecture The constitutional process model is the Elm Architecture: - **State** — typed state shape held by the runtime, not by the view - **Msg** — typed message algebra naming every action a user or system can emit - **Update** — pure reducer of signature `(Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`; describes side effects as `Cmd` values, does not perform them - **View** — pure function of signature `State → ViewTree`; given the same state, produces the same output - **Cmd / Sub** — typed descriptions of side effects to schedule and external sources to subscribe to; interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane The runtime owns the loop: `current State → render View → user emits Msg → Update produces new State and Cmds → runtime interprets Cmds → repeat` This loop is the Elm Architecture. It is the constitutional process model of UX work under this method. --- ## 4A. Process Model Without Language Or Framework Mandate The process model is the Elm Architecture. The implementation stack is the project's choice, recorded in the project's design module. This mirrors `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` §4 ("Functional Bias Without Language Mandate"). The rule is: - the **process model** is constitutional and not negotiable - the **stack** is project-local and free, provided it preserves the model Any realization that preserves §4–§8 is method-compliant. Examples (non-normative): - **A language-integrated reducer runtime** — enables typed state, message, update, command, and view relations as native runtime capabilities. - **A typed reducer with an effect interpreter** — enables a host-language UI stack to preserve pure update and an explicit effect membrane. - **A reactive-signal realization behind a reducer** — enables reactive projection while forbidding signal mutation outside the reducer. - **A server-rendered hypermedia realization** — enables server-side state derivation as the reducer and uses the request/response boundary as the effect membrane. What is constitutionally rejected: any realization that lets the view own state continuation, performs side effects in render code, mutates state outside a typed reducer, or carries multi-step view-local state machines that bypass `Msg`. Two-way binding without `Msg` emission, imperative DOM manipulation in render code, and effect-handlers used as controllers are violations regardless of stack. A project that selects a framework records the choice in its design module along with a short justification of how the framework preserves the §4 process model. The method does not rank frameworks. The method tests realizations against §4–§8. --- ## 5. State Transition Law State changes through typed messages applied by the pure reducer (`Update` of §4). A UX surface declares: - its `State` shape - its `Msg` algebra - its `Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)` - its `Cmd` algebra - its `Sub` algebra when the surface subscribes to external or runtime events Each `Cmd` declaration names: - the effect kind - the typed input payload - the admitted carrier or external boundary it targets - the typed outcome `Msg` family returned to the reducer, including every observed or unresolved effect case possible under the command contract (§6) - the reason and observation carried by each case; a success/failure label alone does not establish completion or absence of effects - any deterministic correlation key required for replay The reducer is pure. It does not perform I/O, log to side channels, or mutate global state. Effects scheduled by `Cmd` are interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane (see §6). View-local ephemera (open/closed flags, hover state, draft input) may be held in implementation-local state cells where the framework provides them, but only when the value is genuinely view-local (not observed by other views, not part of the product's state surface, not consequential after the view unmounts). Product-meaningful state goes through the reducer without exception. The discipline test for whether state belongs in the reducer or in view-local ephemera: if losing the value on unmount changes the product's behavior or another part of the UI's view, it belongs in the reducer. --- ## 6. Effect Membrane Rule Side effects are isolated to a declared effect membrane. The membrane interprets `Cmd` values produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into `Msg` values delivered to the reducer. Inside the membrane: - I/O is allowed - subscriptions to external sources are allowed - imperative interop with the host platform is allowed (DOM, file system, native APIs) Outside the membrane (in render code, in pure helpers consumed by render, in the reducer): - no I/O - no subscriptions - no imperative platform manipulation The membrane has one job: interpret declared `Cmd` values. It is not where logic lives. Branching, conditional state derivation, and multi-step business decisions belong in the reducer; the membrane interprets a single declared `Cmd` per effect. Effect returns distinguish each shared effect state the command can produce as typed `Msg` cases under its contract, including observed non-start and reversal where applicable. The method result records the corresponding shared effect state under the single [effect observation law](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra); it does not replace the UX domain's message algebra. The command binding relates each qualified message to that observation boundary and evidence, preserving missing-reason and unknown cases rather than guessing from a message name. A failed response after dispatch can mean `unknown` effects, not proof of no mutation. Before a dependent repeat, the declared recovery command observes the actual owning state. Reconstructed UI context or an old success message cannot override that observation. This applies [workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) without turning the effect membrane into a second continuation controller. A platform-specific effect handler (whatever name the chosen framework gives it: `useEffect`, `createEffect`, `onMount`, `subscribe`, server-action handler) is part of the membrane only when it interprets a declared `Cmd`. A handler that contains conditional logic deciding state transitions is a method violation. Move the logic to the reducer; let the handler interpret one `Cmd`. --- ## 7. AssetSurface Binding Rule When the product publishes typed asset surfaces (per `ODD_METHOD.md` §11 carrier law and the local product's design), a UX surface binds to one or more `AssetSurface` contracts as its data source and action target. Binding requirements: - the UX surface's `State` is derived from `AssetSurface` projections, not from a UX-local re-declaration of the asset shape - the UX surface's product-truth-changing `Msg` variants map one-to-one to `AssetSurface` action-registry entries or wrap them through a documented projection with no hidden semantic change - UX-local `Msg` variants are reserved for view-local concerns (open/closed, sort order, filter input) - selection within the UX surface emits a Context update (or equivalent) consistent with the product's selection contract - writes from the UX surface go through the `AssetSurface` action registry, not through direct file or service calls This is the rule that produces strong functional consistency between front-end and back-end: the same typed contract is the ground truth on both sides. If the product does not publish `AssetSurface` contracts, the design module must name the equivalent typed contract and apply the same binding law to that contract. Absence of an admitted contract blocks product-truth-changing UX actions. --- ## 8. UX Twin Of ODD §11.5A — View Does Not Own Continuation `ODD_METHOD.md` §11.5A states that ABG owns continuation; the product is a cooperative bounded-step subsystem. The UX twin: **the view does not own state continuation.** State transitions flow through declared `Msg` actions interpreted by the reducer. A view does not: - decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event - chain multiple state updates locally without emitting them as separate `Msg` values - carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures, or module-level variables If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that state machine belongs in the reducer as part of `State`, with explicit `Msg` transitions between phases. The view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is in. The discipline test is the **Msg-replay test**: can you replay the view's behavior by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State`? If the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view. ### 8A. Msg-Replay Proof Requirement Every product UX surface must carry at least one executable Msg-replay proof for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming method closure. A replay proof includes: - an initial `State` fixture - an ordered `Msg` log - the expected final `State` - the expected ordered `Cmd` values - the typed outcome `Msg` values returned by interpreted `Cmd`s, including unresolved effects wherever admitted by the interaction contract - injected deterministic values for time, randomness, generated ids, and external payloads The proof fails if correctness depends on: - DOM state not represented in `State` - mutable refs, module variables, closures, timers, or effect-handler memory - network or file results that bypass typed `Msg` - view-local state that changes product behavior after unmount or replay For a pure projection-only surface, the replay proof may be a no-effect proof: `Msg` log plus final `State` and empty `Cmd` sequence. Each replay assessment returns the shared [result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) on the exact interaction-family predicate, preserving the original test outcome and observed command/effect trace. Evidence of the expected final State, ordered Cmds and typed returns under the declared replay conditions satisfies that replay predicate. A replay can correctly reproduce an unknown-effect Msg without establishing completion of the underlying effect. A demonstrated expected-state or command mismatch, or a demonstrated dependency on any source excluded by this replay contract, is `falsified`; a proof not run retains `not_performed` and cannot satisfy the predicate. Missing decisive trace is `indeterminate`; an unusable fixture or governing basis is `invalid_basis`; an interaction outside the declared assessment domain is `out_of_frame`. Conjoin the required family assessments and other applicable closure checks through [result conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction), retaining failed families and missing coverage. An empty command sequence proves the no-effect predicate only when that is the declared interaction contract. --- ## 9. View Shape Rule A view is a pure function from typed state to a view tree. The view: - accepts typed input (state, props, context) - returns a typed view tree - declares its consumed inputs explicitly - does not capture mutable state in closures across renders - does not read from sources outside its declared input Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived expression, or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body. A view that depends on out-of-render mutation (e.g., a ref written from inside an effect handler and read during render) is a method violation under §6 unless the mutation is part of the declared effect membrane (e.g., a platform handle for imperative interop already named in the design module). --- ## 10. Type Sharing Rule UX-consumed types come from the shared front-end / back-end contract. A UX surface does not re-declare back-end record shapes. It imports them from the shared contract module (typically the same package or a dedicated `contracts/` package). Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam: - HTTP or RPC responses - MCP payloads - file-loaded records - websocket or event-stream messages - agent or worker outputs - URL, storage, clipboard, or browser integration payloads The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so the same type definition is the source of both compile-time types and runtime validators. The mechanism choice is project-local. Compile-time TypeScript alone is not sufficient at these seams. UX-local types are allowed for view-local concerns: form input draft state, sort order enums, filter strings. UX-local types do not shadow back-end types. --- ## 11. Accessibility Minimum A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares: - semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or platform-equivalent affordances) - keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has a pointer interaction - focus management on dynamic content changes - accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks a native semantic equivalent - color contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG AA is the recommended default for web) Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional for internal-only debug surfaces; the design module records the exemption. This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it from their design modules. --- ## 12. Realization Discretion The method is opinionated about the process model. It is not opinionated about the realization stack. The project chooses: - the language - the framework or runtime - the state-container library (if any) - the effect-interpreter mechanism - the runtime validator (if any) - the build, bundling, and deployment toolchain The project records its choices in the design module along with a short justification of how each choice preserves the §4 Elm process model and the §6 effect-membrane rule. The method does not rank stacks. It tests realizations. A realization is method-compliant when §4–§10 hold under inspection and the §14 failure patterns are absent. --- ## 13. Adoption Guidance A project adopts `UX_METHOD.md` by: 1. naming the method in the project's UX-related design modules 2. recording the realization stack choice (per §12) and the justification 3. declaring the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set and structural carrier diagram required by `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` 4. declaring the `State`, `Msg`, `Update`, `Cmd`, and `Sub` shapes for each UX surface in the design module before implementation 5. declaring the `AssetSurface` or equivalent typed-contract bindings (per §7) the surface consumes and emits to 6. naming the effect-membrane mechanism (per §6) and the `Cmd` algebra it interprets 7. naming the executable Msg-replay proof surface required by §8A 8. naming any §11 accessibility refinement the project requires 9. noting any §9 view-shape or §6 effect-membrane exemptions explicitly Adoption is per-project. A project may adopt this method only for some UX surfaces (e.g., the production UI but not internal debug tools), with the scope recorded in the design module. ### 13A. Scaffold And Exemption Law A UX surface is governed by this method by default when any of these are true: - it is reachable from the product shell - it is used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release, or review - it can mutate product truth - it can spawn, attach, resume, or dispatch work - it can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence, or provenance A scaffold, prototype, debug pane, or temporary proof surface may be exempt only when the design module or ticket records: - the exemption scope - the permitted operations - whether mutation is forbidden or explicitly bounded - a visible scaffold/debug label where user-facing - the authoritative surface that will supersede it - the retirement condition and owning ticket - the non-closure condition preventing release if the scaffold remains An exempt scaffold cannot become the production UX by accumulation. It must be retired, repriced into a governed UX surface, or kept outside product closure. ### 13B. UX Sprint Compliance Escrow UX is the primary governed use case for sprint compliance escrow. Under `SPEC_METHOD.md` and `TICKET_METHOD.md`, a UX sprint may defer local UX compliance proof during a short iteration window when per-change proof cost is higher than expected correction cost. This is a cost-optimization rule. It does not weaken the UX process model. A UX sprint may escrow: - screenshots or walkthrough capture - visual review - copy, spacing, density, and layout cleanup - accessibility review and remediation - Msg-replay proof updates for product-meaningful interaction families - design-module wording cleanup - trace cleanup between changed UX states and governing authority A UX sprint may not escrow: - product-truth-changing `Msg` variants that lack an admitted carrier - new or changed `AssetSurface` contracts or equivalent typed product contracts - new navigation, information architecture, or selection authority that changes product meaning - runtime, governance, closure, continuation, lineage, provenance, or evidence semantics - release criteria or method law If one of those appears, the sprint records the finding and the work exits the UX sprint path through standalone repricing or sprint supersession. The UX layer must still not become the hidden constructive carrier. A UX sprint should close when continued iteration is more expensive or less trustworthy than review. Valid close triggers include: - the declared timebox ends - accumulated changed states are too numerous for casual review - screenshots or walkthrough evidence no longer explain the current surface - interaction behavior changed beyond visual polish - reviewer uncertainty makes more iteration unsafe without reconciliation UX sprint close is a forensic walkthrough. The walkthrough reviews each changed screen, state, and product-meaningful interaction against the cited authority. Classify each finding under [Ticket Sprint Close Review](TICKET_METHOD.md#sprint-close-review), which owns the six treatment classes and their reason-sensitive assessment/decision bindings. The UX item-compliance predicate is "this changed screen, state or product-meaningful interaction meets the applicable UX Method and cited design obligations at this basis." Bind its current surface, adopted scope, applicability/exemption evidence and the exact obligations to that owner's map. Apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to the admissibility of this assessment and support; assess UX compliance separately. The treatment and its competent decision authority cannot replace that assessment. Retain the actual failure, uncertainty, performance and effects, including when a local paydown or removal treatment is lawful. Sprint-close eligibility and product UX method closure are separate predicates. The former admits local paydown only under its stated policy. The latter requires its applicable replay and accessibility proof through core conjunction. A recorded authorised exemption decides only its named applicability; an unrecorded exemption supplies no such evidence. Closing the sprint establishes neither discharge of paydown nor method closure. The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where the debt is local to UX realization and the governing method allows follow-up. It may not close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden state continuation, or authority drift remain unclassified. Method closure for a product UX surface still requires the §8A Msg-replay proof and §11 accessibility obligations unless an explicit exemption is recorded. The sprint can defer those obligations during iteration; it cannot erase them. --- ## 14. Failure Pattern A UX surface is violating this method when any of these are true: 1. render code mutates state directly (assignments inside the render body, mutating a prop or context value) 2. view-local state cells carry product-meaningful state instead of view-local ephemera 3. an effect handler contains conditional logic that decides state transitions 4. multi-step state machines live in the view rather than in the reducer 5. mutable refs are read during render outside the declared effect membrane 6. UX-local types shadow or re-declare back-end types instead of importing from the shared contract 7. selection or action emission writes to file or network without going through an `AssetSurface` action 8. view-shape exemptions (per §9) are taken without a recorded design-module entry 9. accessibility is omitted on a public product capability without a recorded exemption 10. two-way binding emits no typed `Msg` action and the reducer is bypassed 11. logic that should be a `Cmd` is implemented imperatively inside an effect handler 12. the view's behavior cannot be replayed by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State` 13. a product-truth-changing UX message has no admitted carrier, graph function, runtime command, or typed product contract 14. external data crosses into UX state without runtime validation 15. a scaffold or debug surface is reachable, mutating, or used as proof without the §13A exemption record 16. a project-local ADR, component convention, or existing code pattern is used to weaken this method 17. a UX sprint claims closure while deferred proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold, or authority debt remains unclassified or un-ticketed Any of these is a method violation. Repeated violations are not normalized by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced. --- ## 15. Review Questions A UX surface review under this method should answer: 1. What is the surface's `State`, `Msg`, and `Update`? 2. What is the surface's `Cmd` and `Sub` algebra? 3. Which `AssetSurface` or equivalent typed contracts does it bind to? 4. Which product-truth-changing messages map to admitted carriers? 5. Where is the effect membrane, and what `Cmd` values does it interpret? 6. Is `View = f(State)` provably pure for this surface? 7. Can the surface's behavior be replayed from a `Msg` log (the §8A Msg-replay proof)? 8. Are all UX-consumed types imported from the shared contract? 9. Are all out-of-process payloads runtime-validated before entering UX state? 10. Are view-shape, effect-membrane, accessibility, scaffold, or debug exemptions documented? 11. What realization stack is chosen, and how does it preserve the §4 Elm process model? 12. Does the surface honor the §8 view-does-not-own-continuation rule under user replay? 13. Does the design module include the `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` carrier set and structural carrier diagram required for closure? 14. If the work used a UX sprint, did close review classify every deferred proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold, and authority finding? If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete. --- ## 16. Relationship To Other Method Surfaces - `SPEC_METHOD.md` governs constitutional process, authority flow, repricing, and migration law. - `ODD_METHOD.md` governs graph-native constructive carrier law. UX surfaces are projection / query surfaces under §10 of that method. - `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` governs deterministic realization discipline at the module level. `UX_METHOD.md` refines it for UX modules. - `TICKET_METHOD.md` governs ticket and sprint lifecycle. UX work may use sprint compliance escrow under §13B when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof visible, bounded, and payable. - `WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` governs world-model semantic law for products that have a world-model dimension. UX surfaces over world-model state still bind through `AssetSurface` (or equivalent) per §7. A UX-touching design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` plus `UX_METHOD.md`. A non-UX design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` only and ignores this surface. --- ## 17. Non-Goals `UX_METHOD.md` is not: - a styling guide or design system specification - a component library - a brand or visual-identity surface - a wireframing or prototyping process - a research method for user studies - a stack ranking or framework recommendation Those are valid concerns; they belong in product-local surfaces, not in this constitutional method. --- ## 18. Canonical Compression `UX_METHOD.md` adopts the **Elm Architecture** as the constitutional UX process model and refines `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` for UX surfaces. The model: typed `State` held by the runtime, typed `Msg` algebra, pure `Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`, pure `View : State → ViewTree`, side effects as `Cmd` values interpreted at a declared effect membrane that returns `Msg` to the reducer. The view does not own continuation (UX twin of `ODD_METHOD.md` §11.5A); the **Msg-replay test** is the discipline check. The realization stack is the project's choice, recorded in the design module along with justification of model preservation. The method tests realizations against §4–§10 and the §14 failure patterns; it does not rank stacks, languages, or frameworks. When adopted, this method is the sole UX realization authority for the covered surface. Product-truth-changing UX messages must map to admitted product carriers; the UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. External payloads are runtime-validated before entering UX state. Scaffolds and debug surfaces are governed unless explicitly exempted, bounded, and retired. UX sprints may defer local proof and cleanup only as visible compliance escrow; close review must classify and pay down the debt before method closure is claimed.

40	criteria remain at their owner; selecting this view grants no acceptance.

47	SPEC_METHOD enclosing-admission owner. These selections follow the task's

55	|---|---|

57	| Generic frame law: declaration, evaluation and composition | [Reference Frame Method](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md); [Spec semantic resolution](SPEC_METHOD.md#bounded-context-semantic-resolution) owns bounded-context term resolution |

115	this entry creates no alternative continuation owner. The projected frames are
